chunks: and the aged who have no means (for livelihood),
nor are they ready for begging.
This is heavy on the officers;
in fact, every right is heavy.
Allāh lightens it for those who seek the next world and so they endure (hardships) upon themselves,
and trust on the truthfulness of Allāh’s promise to them.
ai.seo_question: What are the duties of a governor towards orphans and the elderly according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali frames the administration of orphans (al-yatama) and the humble (dhawu al-riqqa) as a heavy trust (thiqal) on the governor, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social justice and the ruler's accountability to the vulnerable. This burden is alleviated through sabr (patience) and tawakkul (trust in God's promise), linking administrative duty to spiritual discipline. The passage underscores that caring for those who do not actively seek aid is a distinct marker of a just ruler's diligence.
